title: Lesson 3 — Literacy Acquisition Elements
source: User-supplied WGU Lesson 3 introduction, objective, and guided practice
lesson_summary: Effective literacy acquisition requires a comprehensive understanding and application of phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension strategies tailored to learners across age groups. The introduction connects lexical quality of words and oral language to language acquisition.

items.prompt: Which of the following is a key element of literacy acquisition?
items.feedback_correct: Decoding skills involve the ability to identify written symbols into spoken sounds and language.
items.assessment_quality_flag: AMBIGUOUS: Vocabulary building, phonological awareness, and decoding are all plausible elements of literacy acquisition. Keep the original source answer for faithful transcription but do not use this item as a strict single-correct independent mastery assessment until rewritten or reviewed.

items.prompt: Which of the following is an essential aspect of literacy acquisition?
items.feedback_correct: Comprehension strategies are crucial for understanding and interpreting text, which is a fundamental part of literacy acquisition.
